Long sticks with diagonal scores and a blistered skin. Steam in the oven is what helps those ears lift.

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 66% hydration, 2% salt, and 0.8% yeast. The dough wants folds and steam, not a tight sandwich loaf. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast until no dry flour remains. At 66% hydration the dough is soft and a bit sticky. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk with folds Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 2 to 2.5 hours. During the first 90 minutes, give it three stretch-and-folds, about 30 minutes apart. It is ready when it has grown by about half and looks bubbly.
  3. Divide Tip it onto a lightly floured counter and cut three or four sticks. With 500 g of flour the dough is one batch of home-length baguettes, not one huge loaf.
  4. Preshape Gently tighten each piece into a short log. Cover them and rest 20 to 30 minutes so they stop pulling back.
  5. Shape Flatten each log, fold the long sides in, and roll it out to the length of your baking sheet or cloth. The seam goes down. A tight skin is what lets the scores open.
  6. Proof Set them seam-side down in the folds of a floured cloth for 40 to 60 minutes at about 24°C (75°F), until a finger press springs back slowly.
  7. Score and bake Heat the oven to 240°C (465°F) with a tray for steam. Make four or five diagonal cuts. Bake 12 minutes with steam, then uncover or vent, lower the oven to 220°C (425°F), and bake 12 to 15 minutes more, until the crust is deep brown and the cuts have opened.
  8. Cool Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes. The crust softens a little as it cools, and the center finishes setting.
